Here are the outcome candidates, taken from the spec's rulings (§3, R1–R11). The order below is the spec's order, not a ranking.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome: what you get | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index catalog covering archived quarters over a range you choose | R1, §4.2 | Data volume can't be estimated until you pick the range. §4.8 assumes no start year. `full-index/` runs from 1993 Q1, so the worst case is about 135 quarterly files. At the 3 req/s target, requests are trivial; transfer size dominates. The core stage measures it. |
| O2 | Daily indexes added as they appear, with catch-up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2, §4.2 | About 250 files a year (business days only), small per file. Requests are negligible against the budget. |
| O3 | Parsed, validated, deduplicated rows in Parquet, with provenance for each row | R3, §4.4–4.5 | Compute and peak memory per quarter are unknown. §7 step 4 asks for them to be recorded, so the core stage measures them. |
| O4 | Re-running a parser change from stored original bytes, with no new download | R6 | Storage roughly equal to all bytes downloaded for O1 and O2. No SEC traffic. |
| O5 | Weekly re-reads of closed quarters that apply additions and field changes automatically, and hold removals until you approve them | R7, R10, §4.4 | Each week re-downloads every supported quarter, so about the full O1 volume per week. Your time goes to approving each withdrawal candidate. |
| O6 | Readers only ever see complete quarter versions, through one active pointer | R9, §4.6 | Not material. |
| O7 | All SEC traffic shares one identified request budget: 3 req/s, no bursts, one active collector | R8, R11, §4.3 | Not material. It caps throughput at 3 req/s, below the SEC's published 10. |
| O8 | Scheduled operation on Azure, with monitoring, alerts and runbooks | R4, §4.7–4.9 | Azure spend can't be estimated: region, sizes and retention are deployment values (§4.8). The stage that deploys measures it. |

## Track

**One track, a known progression.** I considered splitting off O8, the Azure operation, because the catalog works without Azure. I kept it in because O8 doesn't stand without the catalog, so they aren't unrelated questions. Spec §7 already names the progression, from local fixtures through smoke test, backfill, daily trigger, reconciliation and scheduled runs. So I'd commit every stage from first to last.

Under the skill's rules, the core stage would run on one real quarter at the smallest usable standard. It would leave out manifests, pointers, the withdrawal gate and Azure, each placed in a named later stage.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, in a uv workspace.
- Platform R4: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS and Table Storage. Both the ADR and the spec are still **Proposed**, so I'm recording this as chosen, pending acceptance.
- R5: backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation share one downloader, parser and publisher.
- R11 / §4.8: the stated defaults are starting values.
- CI never downloads from the SEC (§6).
- §2.2's out-of-scope list stands.
- Code goes in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (§4.9). The scaffold also has `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, which the spec doesn't mention. I'll leave them unclaimed unless you assign them.

## Roadmap name

`specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. When there's a spec, the name is its filename stem used whole.

## Your call

**Please rank O1–O8, and confirm or change the track, its kind, the package assignment and the name.**

Optionally, I can run one small probe to firm up O1's cost: fetch one recent quarter's `full-index` listing and its `master.idx` size. That's two requests, read-only. Say yes if you want it.
